lyrics:
[Intro: open-chord guitar riff with gaps, hi-hat counting]

[Verse 1: cheeky rasp, drums and bass kick in]
Packed a bag and I kissed the cat
Left a note where the fridge is at
Don't need a map, don't need a plan
Got a full tank and a bad idea, man

[Pre-Chorus: chords climb, snare builds]
Ask me where I'm going
I'm going where it's going

[Chorus: gang vocals, ringing chords]
I'm on a shortcut to trouble
Shortcut to trouble
Tell my mother I was last seen smiling
Shortcut to trouble

[Verse 2: cheeky rasp, riff underneath]
Sold the mower and I kept the amp
Phone's on silent in a glovebox camp
My doctor said to take it slow
I said "sure, Doc," and I let it go

[Pre-Chorus: chords climb, snare builds]
Ask me where I'm going
I'm going where it's going

[Chorus: gang vocals, ringing chords]
I'm on a shortcut to trouble
Shortcut to trouble
Tell my mother I was last seen smiling
Shortcut to trouble

[Guitar Solo: bluesy, biting, short]

[Bridge: band drops to kick drum and gang shout]
And I'm going all the way
(All the way)
And I'm not coming back till Tuesday
(Tuesday)

[Final Chorus: full band, lead guitar over the top]
I'm on a shortcut to trouble
Shortcut to trouble
Tell my mother I was last seen smiling
Shortcut to trouble
Shortcut to trouble

[Outro: riff, one last chord, a laugh]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 116 BPM, 4/4, A major. A swaggering, mid-tempo boogie with space in it. Good-humoured and loud.

VOICE: Male, a high, raspy, cheeky rock voice with a wink in every line, half sung and half leered, never screamed. A gang of rough male voices shouts the title in the chorus and answers in the bridge.

INSTRUMENTS: Two electric guitars with a crunchy, lightly overdriven tone: one plays the open-chord riff with deliberate silences, the other doubles it and takes a short, biting, blues-based solo. A simple, solid bass on the root notes. A dry, heavy drum kit playing the plainest possible beat. No keyboards.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the riff alone with the hi-hat. 0:14 Verse 1, the band in. 0:35 Pre-chorus. 0:44 Chorus 1. 1:02 Verse 2. 1:23 Pre-chorus. 1:32 Chorus 2. 1:50 Guitar solo. 2:12 Bridge, kick drum and shouting. 2:30 Final chorus with lead guitar on top. 3:05 Outro, the riff, a final chord and a laugh at 3:25.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1970s hard rock: dry, punchy and uncluttered, two guitars panned apart, drums natural, plenty of room between the notes.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The silences in the opening riff.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The rebel has sold his lawnmower and ignored his doctor, and intends to be back by Tuesday. It is the same grin on an older face, and a third, different angle from the two other songs in this series inspired by the same band.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Mischief from start to finish.
